I've never understood why he was sorted into a house that values loyalty and courage. He is by far the least loyal and most cowardly character in the series, so why did the Sorting Hat put him here?
Why was Peter Pettigrew a Gryffindor?

When I was reading the books as a kid I justified his being in Gryffindor because he might have asked to be placed there and the Sorting Hat just sort allowed that to happen like it did with Harry (and maybe Neville but unlike Neville Peter didn't turn out brave at all).

It was either that or he was brave but like some people do he cracked under the eventual pressure and lost that part of him. I mean he had to have some balls if he was hanging out with the Marauders and worked to become an animagus which is supposed to be dangerous.

Another layer off that second idea I considered was maybe at some point he had the potential to become courageous and loyal but his life just strayed from that path that the Sorting Hat sensed. This idea came up to me because Hermione, at least I thought, should have been put into Ravenclaw. She certainly at the start of the books was more Ravenclaw than Gryffindor; however as the book progressed she grew into the bravery and courage seen in a typical Gryffindor. Same can be said about Harry and Slytherin.

Courage isn't just having the guts to do good things. He had courage. He joined the Death Eaters which took courage to abandon his friends. Obviously it was a terrible thing but that doesn't mean it wasn't courageous.

He had the courage to run around with Lupin in his werewolf form for years. He had the courage to spy on the Order of the Phoenix for the Death Eaters. These actions also show his loyalty and bravery, which is what sets Gryffindors apart.

Gryffindors will do terrible things if they believe it is the right thing to do. Hagrid tried to transfigure Dudley into a pig because Dudley was being rude. Hermione cast a full body-bind curse on Neville because he was going to stop the trio from leaving their tower and losing Gryffindor points. Peter also did terrible things but he believed them to be right because he had a poor moral compass. He showed courage and bravery in carrying out these acts and loyalty to the Death Eaters and Voldemort.

There can be bad Gryffindors, just like there can be good Slytherins. Peter had the potential to do good but chose not to. He still displayed Gryffindor traits, just not in a good way

Hey Arith! You're certainly on the right track. The fix will be either of the possible answers you've noted!

I would first look for an unhooked washer line. If you look on the back of the nozzle under the hood, you should see some black rubber hose going to it. Since one is working and the other is not (they share the same pump), if there is a blockage in the line, it will occur after the branch. Replacing this line is easy and cheap! You may use regular vacuum hose found at any auto parts shop.

Now for the nozzle. If you look closely at the nozzle, you may be able to spot some buildup on it. Using computer cleaner against the nozzle will sometimes clear the blockage. If you can take the clogged nozzle off, soaking it in distilled vinegar will clear build-up in no time! Finally, replacement of the nozzle will most likely be somewhere around 10 pounds for you.
vinegar works fast, for the lazy start using distilled water instead of washer fluid. It will slowly dissolve the buildup in the washer jet.
